claims.statement: For user interface components, name and role are programmatically determinable; user-settable states, properties, and values are programmatically settable; change notification is available to user agents including assistive technologies.
exclusions: does not prescribe one universal widget implementation

claims.statement: When a control has a visible text label, its accessible name contains that text subject to the Success Criterion exceptions.
exclusions: does not require every accessible name to be visible

claims.statement: When sequential navigation order affects meaning or operation, focusable components receive focus in an order that preserves meaning and operability.
exclusions: does not prescribe DOM order as the only implementation

claims.statement: Text and images of text meet the WCAG 2.2 minimum contrast ratios subject to the stated large-text, incidental, and logotype exceptions.
exclusions: does not apply the normal-text ratio to exempt content

claims.statement: Visual information needed to identify user interface components and states meets the WCAG 2.2 non-text contrast criterion subject to its exceptions.
exclusions: does not treat inactive components as in-scope when the criterion excludes them

claims.statement: Except for captions and images of text, text can be resized up to 200 percent without loss of content or functionality.
exclusions: does not claim that browser zoom and text-only resize are identical mechanisms

claims.statement: Ordinary content can be presented without loss of information or functionality and without two-dimensional scrolling at the criterion's stated dimensions, except for content requiring two-dimensional layout for usage or meaning.
exclusions: preserves the two-dimensional-layout exception

claims.statement: A custom control exposes an applicable non-abstract WAI-ARIA role with the semantics and required properties defined for that role.
claims.scope: WAI-ARIA 1.2 role model and role definitions
exclusions: does not use abstract roles
does not override conflicting strong native semantics

claims.statement: Applicable WAI-ARIA states and properties expose the current control state or value according to their defined semantics and allowed values.
exclusions: does not invent a property unsupported by the chosen role

claims.statement: Accessible names are computed from referenced author labels, aria-label, host-language labeling, or name-from-content according to the normative precedence algorithm.
claims.scope: Accessible Name and Description Computation 1.1 section 4.3
exclusions: does not treat placeholder or visual position as a stable label without a conforming name source

claims.statement: Identify dependency failure modes and place an explicit isolation or degradation boundary so the failure affects only a limited component set while the component preserves its critical function where possible.
exclusions: does not prescribe cells for every workload
does not claim every dependency can be softened

claims.statement: Set a realistic caller deadline and, when a server makes downstream RPCs for that call, propagate the original deadline as a timeout with elapsed time deducted so downstream work cannot outlive the caller's budget.
claims.scope: gRPC Deadlines guide, Deadlines on the Client and Deadline Propagation
exclusions: does not prescribe one numeric timeout for all calls
does not claim every transport propagates deadlines automatically

claims.statement: Before automatic retries, verify the service operation is idempotent; bound retries by a maximum attempt count or elapsed-time limit and choose timeouts and stop conditions for the use case.
exclusions: does not make a non-idempotent operation safe by adding backoff
does not prescribe one universal attempt count

claims.statement: A circuit breaker monitors downstream call failures, stops sending requests when failures are sufficiently high, and later admits limited probes to test whether the downstream system recovered.
claims.scope: AWS Well-Architected REL05-BP01, Implementation steps item 2
exclusions: does not open solely because one caller is unwilling to wait
does not prescribe one universal failure threshold or probe interval

claims.statement: Define RTO from acceptable service-restoration delay and RPO from acceptable data loss, then select a recovery, replication, standby, or active-active strategy that can meet those objectives within explicit cost and complexity constraints.
exclusions: does not claim active-active is universally preferable
does not equate replication alone with protection from corruption

claims.statement: Recovery evidence must include controlled component-loss or failover exercises and restored-data validation that checks availability, accessibility, and corruption, rather than proving only that a host can be replaced.
exclusions: does not authorize unguarded production fault injection
does not treat backup existence as proof of recoverability

claims.statement: When not all work can be served, identify the component's core business function and preserve its most critical functionality while degrading or dropping less critical work according to explicit business requirements.
exclusions: does not infer request value without a stated business criticality
does not permit dropping correctness requirements that define the core function

claims.statement: When overload or a dependency failure prevents normal work, return an explicit throttling, failure, or partial-result indication that the caller can handle; do not present silently omitted work as a normal complete result.
exclusions: does not require one universal HTTP status for non-HTTP protocols
does not claim every optional field must be returned during degradation

claims.statement: All functionality is operable through a keyboard interface without individual-keystroke timing requirements, except where the underlying function depends on the path of movement.
exclusions: Does not require every pointer control to have a one-to-one keyboard control when equivalent functionality is available.
Preserves the path-dependent-function exception.

claims.statement: Web content does not restrict input modalities available on the platform except where essential, required for security, or required to respect user settings.
exclusions: Preserves the essential, security, and user-setting exceptions.

claims.statement: Color is not the only visual means of conveying information, indicating an action, prompting a response, or distinguishing a visual element.
exclusions: Does not prohibit using color as an additional cue.

claims.statement: When an input error is automatically detected, the item in error is identified and the error is described to the user in text.
exclusions: Does not itself require a correction suggestion when one is unknown.

claims.statement: Information, structure, and relationships conveyed through presentation are programmatically determinable or available in text.
exclusions: Does not mandate one particular association attribute.

claims.statement: When a host-language feature with identical role semantics and values is available and there is no compelling reason to avoid it, authors should use the host-language feature instead of repurposing another element with WAI-ARIA.
exclusions: Does not claim a native control is sufficient when its semantics or values do not match the required interaction.

claims.statement: aria-errormessage identifies the element containing an object's error message and is used with aria-invalid when that message is pertinent.
exclusions: Does not claim aria-errormessage is supported on a role that does not permit it.
Does not replace the requirement that the error be available as visible text when WCAG 3.3.1 applies.

claims.statement: The accessibility of interactive content cannot be confirmed by static checks alone.
exclusions: Does not prescribe one browser, assistive technology, or automated tool matrix.
Does not establish a performance-testing claim.

claims.statement: Developers of interactive content should test device-independent access and verify accessibility API access to all content and changes during user interaction.
exclusions: Does not prove a specific screen reader and browser combination without observed evidence.

claims.statement: Isolate domain-model expression and business logic from UI, persistence, application, and infrastructure concerns so domain objects do not display or store themselves.
exclusions: does not by itself identify commands or queries
does not prescribe a framework

claims.statement: Model an object as an entity when identity and lifecycle continuity distinguish it even while attributes or representations change.
exclusions: does not equate persistence-generated keys with domain identity in every model

claims.statement: Model a concept as a value object when only attributes and related logic matter; give it no identity and treat it as immutable with side-effect-free operations.
exclusions: does not apply when independent identity or lifecycle continuity is required

claims.statement: An entity is responsible for tracking its state and the rules regulating its lifecycle.
exclusions: does not move unrelated application orchestration or persistence behavior into the entity

claims.statement: Define aggregate-wide properties and invariants, assign enforcement to the aggregate root or designated mechanism, use the same aggregate boundary for transactions, enforce within it synchronously, and handle cross-boundary updates asynchronously.
exclusions: does not authorize temporary invariant violation inside the aggregate
does not claim all related objects belong to one aggregate

claims.statement: A repository offers domain-meaningful selection and returns fully instantiated domain objects, collections, or aggregate proxies while encapsulating storage and query technology.
exclusions: does not expose database query mechanics to domain callers
does not require a repository for every type

claims.statement: A downstream system can protect its own domain model by placing an isolating layer at the upstream boundary that translates between the upstream and downstream models.
exclusions: does not make upstream names, types, or error semantics part of the downstream domain model

claims.statement: For protobuf integrations whose clients and servers roll out independently, do not reuse tag numbers or casually change field types; reserve deleted numbers and names to preserve stored and in-flight compatibility.
exclusions: does not generalize to every serialization format
does not make provider field names domain vocabulary

claims.statement: For HTTP Problem Details, consumers use the type URI as the primary problem identifier; problem details expose the HTTP interface, not underlying implementation or a replacement for an existing domain-specific error format.
exclusions: does not make a provider problem type a core-domain failure type
does not authorize exposing implementation internals

claims.statement: Automatic HTTP retry depends on idempotent request semantics, and Retry-After explicitly communicates when a follow-up request ought to occur.
claims.scope: RFC 9110 HTTP retry and idempotency semantics
exclusions: does not imply every provider error is retryable
does not define domain recovery policy
